story.value: Scandium's name comes from the Latin word scandia, meaning Scandinavia, where the mineral was found.
Scandium was discovered by the Swedish chemist Lars-Fredrik Nilson.
The Swedish chemist Per Theodore Cleve proved that scandium was the element eka-boron that Mendeleev had predicted.

uses.value: Alloys of scandium and aluminum are used in some sports equipment, such as baseball bats, bicycle frames and lacrosse sticks.
Scandium oxide, also known as scandia, is used to make high intensity lights.
Scandium iodide is added to mercury vapor lamps so that their light closely resembles sunlight.
Mercury vapor lamps with added scandium iodide give light resembling sunlight, which is important for indoor or night-time color TV.
